headline: Google has kept its most powerful AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, away from the public and given it only to vetted cybersecurity experts because hackers could misuse it.
score_reason: Event dates from 30 Sep 2026, so the story is stale; lowered by 2 from 7.
importance_line: The public and ordinary companies cannot yet use Google's strongest model, while vetted cyber-defenders and the US government can; the story is over two weeks old and dated.
summary: The Guardian reports that Google said on 30 September 2026 it would not release Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model, to the public for now, giving it only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts so hackers cannot misuse it. Google chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu called a phased release necessary, and Google said it also gave the US government early access.
notes: The IOL page was blocked; the story was read at The Guardian, which is the outlet credited. The IOL link carries a 1 Oct 2026 date, so the event is older than the window. Score lowered from 7 to 5 as stale.
